articleTitle: Highly efficient energy metering and trend analysis techniques for maximum control
publicationTitle: [Proceedings] IEEE 1992 Annual Textile, Fiber and Film Industry Technical Conference
abstract: Metering/monitoring is a method used to obtain energy data while the trend analysis process is a method of converting data to useful information in the form of graphical and report output. The techniques of analysis using energy invoices, and unmetered energy consumption data, are discussed. Other optics covered include the evolution of metering and trending systems and their justification. Six reasons to meter energy are provided. The fundamentals of flow metering are noted, as are personal computer energy software and its applications. The ultimate goal of a metering and trending system is to assist the plant or facility in managing the energy required to produce a specific product of service. Monitoring and trending energy consumption allows for close control while minimizing expenses.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Optimizing plant performance through power distribution monitoring
publicationTitle: [Proceedings] IEEE 1992 Annual Textile, Fiber and Film Industry Technical Conference
abstract: The introduction of the microprocessor into metering, protection and control products throughout the power distribution system has provided stand-alone devices with the ability to communicate the information used to perform their standard functions back to a central monitoring point cost effectively. The author focuses on the benefits to overall plant productivity and efficiency as a result of these devices and their inexpensive communication capabilities. Topics covered include device evolution, communications the value of monitoring using so-called smart devices, and the cost of power monitoring.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: PLC vs DCS in process control-the distinction is fading
publicationTitle: [Proceedings] IEEE 1992 Annual Textile, Fiber and Film Industry Technical Conference
abstract: It is argued that with the advent of new software tools, which provide integrated process control programming to the programmable logic control (PLC) and ladder logic programming to the distributed control system (DCS), the issue of which is appropriate must be made on a project by project basis. The consideration is no longer one of how many digital inputs and outputs there are versus the number of analog I/O points. It is to be based instead on price, type of operator interface and the complexity of functionality, and degree of local support.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Industrial power considerations for variable speed drives (VSD's)
publicationTitle: [Proceedings] IEEE 1992 Annual Textile, Fiber and Film Industry Technical Conference
abstract: It is argued that electronic variable speed drives (VSDs) are the preferred choice for industrial AC-motor speed control. Offering advantages over their mechanical counterparts, the VSDs can provide improved efficiency and flexibility, enhanced product quality, a higher degree of accuracy and computer compatibility. However, they are more sensitive to power line disturbances such as transients, harmonics, voltage variations and momentary interruptions. These concerns must be addressed at the time a VSD installation is designed and installed in order to avoid future problems with both the VSD and other plant electronic equipment.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Liability and professional issues facing engineers in industry
publicationTitle: [Proceedings] IEEE 1992 Annual Textile, Fiber and Film Industry Technical Conference
abstract: The liability of industrial engineers and the pros and cons of professional registration are discussed. The rewards and risks of moonlighting are examined along with new developments in so-called good Samaritan legislation. The history of professional liability is sketched and general definitions are given for criminal law, civil law, torts and negligence. Other topics covered include standards of practice, registration, industrial exemption, and licensing issues.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Starting now-a review of reduced voltage AC motor starters
publicationTitle: [Proceedings] IEEE 1992 Annual Textile, Fiber and Film Industry Technical Conference
abstract: The wide acceptance of variable frequency (VF) AC drives in textile, fiber and film applications has led to their use to control motor starting performance, even where the motor is run at a constant speed. The benefit of a VF drive in such applications lies primarily in its ability to provide a gentle start, in which the torque applied to the load and the inrush current from the power line are not allowed to interfere with the process or with adjacent equipment. The technology used in a VF drive, which draws power from the line, converts it to DC and inverts it to AC at a different voltage and frequency, can also control voltage alone. The author describes solid state and electromechanical starters, and VF drives. Performance during and after a start are discussed, as is performance when stopping. A brief overview of available accessories for overcurrent protection diagnostics and enclosures is given. General trouble-shooting and spare parts issues are also noted. Applications and future trends are briefly considered.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Voltage selection for large horsepower AC motors
publicationTitle: [Proceedings] IEEE 1992 Annual Textile, Fiber and Film Industry Technical Conference
abstract: When installing large horse-power motors in manufacturing facilities, the question of which voltage to specify often arises. In most instances, there are many options to choose from. Several case studies of new and existing textile facilities are used to set forth some basic design and economic considerations in order to help determine which voltage to specify.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Considerations for the use of AC induction motors on variable frequency controllers in high performance applications
publicationTitle: [Proceedings] IEEE 1992 Annual Textile, Fiber and Film Industry Technical Conference
abstract: Until recently the majority of AC variable speed drives have been applied to variable torque, pump and fan applications. Advances in drive technology have led to the use of induction motors in high performance applications that exceed the capability of motors designed for operation on sine-wave power. These applications, which have traditionally been served by DC systems, have created the need for definite purpose AC induction motors designed specifically for operation on adjustable frequency controllers. A discussion is presented of the considerations for a successful application and the limitations of standard motor designs are highlighted.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Dumb stunts not to repeat. . .neat tricks to use again (industrial installation, safety)
publicationTitle: [Proceedings] IEEE 1992 Annual Textile, Fiber and Film Industry Technical Conference
abstract: The author presents an overview of accidents, mistakes, and problems along with suggestions for improvements within industrial settings. This anecdotal material covers the gamut of topics with which an engineer may become involved. In particular the author covers electrical installation, transformers, electric conduits, engineering drawings, and CAD.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
